paper-1-non-fiction-texts-and-transactio: The text never says she's afraid. How do you know she is?
Slim, skinny, scrawny: same body. Why three different verdicts?
One word. Full stop. Why does a sentence that short land so hard?
One city, two writers, no feelings stated. How do you spot attitude?
Two writers, two centuries, one school day. Compare what, or how?
Why does admitting the other side has a point make you stronger?
One opinion, a letter or a speech. What has to change?
paper-2-poetry-and-prose-texts-and-imagi: Why does "Disabled" keep jumping between then and now?
Told her husband is dead, she goes upstairs alone. What does she feel?
One borrowed necklace, ten years of debt. Who is really to blame?
Many exam stories go wrong in one place. Beginning, middle or end?
A busy market, without the word 'busy'. Where do you point the camera?
Your teacher can't correct your draft. How do you find the weak bit?
component-3-spoken-language-endorsement: A few minutes, a room of classmates. What makes them listen on?
Same talk, Pass or Distinction. What changes besides the words?
An unexpected question. What do strong speakers do next?
